Hi Sara — thanks for the specific questions. Below is a concise feature matrix and some technical notes. Happy to join a call to walk through any item.

Feature matrix (quick view):
- Hosted (standard):
  * In-transit: TLS 1.2+; termination at Redwood edge.
  * At-rest: envelope encryption with Redwood-managed root keys.
  * CMK/BYOK: not enabled by default; enterprise customers can request a restricted CMK flow (envelope keys encrypted by a customer-provided KMS key) — works for limited tenants after procurement/contracting + security review.
  * HSM: Hosted root keys are HSM-backed in our KMS provider, but we do not provide customer-controlled HSM in the fully-managed Hosted tier.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  * In-transit: TLS 1.2+; optional mTLS.
  * At-rest: envelope encryption; primary root key can be customer-managed via customer KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault).
  * CMK/BYOK: supported — keys remain in your cloud KMS; Redwood stores only encrypted key material (envelope).
  * HSM: if your cloud KMS is HSM-backed (e.g., AWS CloudHSM-backed KMS), then keys are HSM-protected and never exported.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  * In-transit: configurable; mTLS supported.
  * At-rest: full control — you can configure local HSM or KMS and bring keys on-prem.
  * CMK/BYOK: full BYOK with HSM-backed options; Redwood's control plane can be configured to never access plaintext keys.

Technical notes:
- Envelope encryption is standard: data keys are generated per-tenant and wrapped by the configured root CMK. Rotation: keys can be rotated with zero-downtime rewrap of new encryptions; historical ciphertext remains readable with previous keys.
- Key export: for Dedicated/Private, exported keys are not required. We rely on cloud KMS APIs (Encrypt/Decrypt) or HSM-local signing operations.
- Auditability: we push key usage logs (KMS API call & request ids) into the customer's logging destination for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can request redacted audit exports under contract.
- HIPAA/BAA: Redwood offers a BAA for Dedicated and Private customers. We can accommodate HIPAA workloads after BAA execution and an initial security intake.
- SOC 2 access: we provide a read-only portal for SOC 2 Type II to customers who complete an NDA; portal link and instructions included in Hannah's attachment.

Attachments: I can produce a one-page matrix PDF comparing Host/Dedicated/Private options (I will attach the file after internal review).

If helpful, proposed next step: 30-min technical alignment focused on keys and auditability this Thursday 9-9:30am PT. Does that work for your team?
